props.gloss_en: the baraita: any animal that chews the cud is known to have no upper teeth, and is kosher
a young camel has no cuspids either
rather, this is what [the baraita] says: any animal that has no upper teeth is known to chew the cud and part the hoof, and is kosher
[the tooth sign is for] where its hooves were cut
Rav Chisda: one walking in the wilderness who found an animal whose hooves were cut inspects its mouth: if it has no upper teeth it is known to be kosher; if not, it is known to be non-kosher
Rav Chisda: provided he recognizes a camel
rather: provided he recognizes a young camel

the school of R' Yishmael: 'the camel, for it chews the cud' (Lev 11:4) -- the Ruler of His world knows there is nothing that chews the cud and is non-kosher but the camel; therefore the verse specified it with 'it'

supports.gloss_en: וכדרב חסדא -- as Rav Chisda: an animal found with cut hooves is inspected by its mouth
דתני דבי רבי ישמעאל -- 'it': only the camel chews the cud and is non-kosher, so no other species defeats the mouth inspection

objections.gloss_en: וכללא הוא? והרי גמל -- it chews the cud, has no upper teeth, and is non-kosher!

answered_by.gloss_en: גמל ניבי אית ליה -- a camel has cuspids (= p_gamal_nivei)

objections.gloss_en: והרי בן גמל -- a young camel has no cuspids either, and is non-kosher (not answered: the stam re-reads the baraita instead)
ותו, הרי שפן וארנבת -- they chew the cud and have upper teeth, and are non-kosher (not answered: the stam re-reads the baraita instead)
ועוד, שינים מי כתיבי באורייתא? -- teeth are not written in the Torah, yet the baraita lists them as the Torah's sign (not answered: the stam re-reads the baraita instead)
גמל ניבי אית ליה! -- a camel has cuspids, so the mouth inspection already excludes it (not answered: the proviso is emended to the young camel, p_chisda_makir_ben_gamal)
לאו אמרת איכא בן גמל? איכא נמי מינא אחרינא דדמי לבן גמל! -- perhaps another species resembles the young camel

answered_by.gloss_en: לא סלקא דעתך -- the school of R' Yishmael: only the camel chews the cud and is non-kosher (= p_dvei_ri_hu_gamal)
